title: notification-04: Toast Action Dispatch
summary: Azioni toast dispatchate tramite ActionRegistry/policy path.
description: NotificationDismissOne{id}/All/Last e NotificationPick: naming/build_action/priority/policy Global/registry/descriptor/keybinding. Handler di on_action(id,key) -> lookup in actions:Vec by key -> fire Intent via layer_emitter (nessuna variante AppEvent bespoke).
goals: Il dismiss passa per tre WmAction reali; l'azione inline di un toast risolve on_action(id,key) e spara il suo Intent; notification.pick apre uno scoped picker aggiuntivo al pool globale prefix+/.
dependencies: Il wiring di on_action/on_dismiss verso layer_emitter richiede il mount ToastStack (P060), non ancora costruito.
completionCriteria: Le tre azioni di dismiss + NotificationPick cablate end-to-end e verificate con cargo check (fatto)
Handler reale di on_action(id,key) via layer_emitter (non fatto, aspetta il mount)

tasks.title: Handle notification action event through registry path
tasks.description:
Al ricevere `on_action(id, key)` dallo `ToastStack`: cercare la `NotificationAction` corrispondente a `key` tra `actions: Vec<...>` della notifica `id`, clonarne l'`Intent`, applicare `dismiss_after` se richiesto, e sparare l'Intent tramite `chrome::layer_emitter` — riusa il path generico esistente (`AppEvent::ChromeIntent`), nessuna variante bespoke (vedi T211/T212, eliminati: erano superflui).

---
**Completion summary:**
SHIPPED: handle_notification_action_relay (heca/src/handlers.rs) + WmAction::NotificationActionRelay{notification_id,key} (new variant, full checklist: build_action/priority/policy Global/registry/descriptor). On receipt: looks up the NotificationAction by key via new NotificationRuntime::action_and_dismiss_after_for_visible (returns (Intent, bool) in one call), fires the cloned Intent through chrome::layer_emitter (reusing state.notification_layer_id set at mount, T203) — same generic AppEvent::ChromeIntent path everything else uses, no bespoke variant — then dismisses the notification if dismiss_after was true. The widget's on_action(id,key) closure (in chrome/notification_layer.rs) posts this relay by name since the real intent cannot be known at mount time (the notification doesn't exist yet). VERIFICATION: cargo check -p heca clean; ./scripts/lint-changed.sh test green (643 tests, 0 failures, confirmed in the run before this fix; this change only added a method + a call site, re-checked with cargo check after); ./scripts/lint-changed.sh clean for heca (0 warnings — heca-grid-ui's 2 warnings are pre-existing in code I did not touch). NOT verified: nothing on screen — needs Antonio to raise a notification with an action and click it. FILES: heca/src/handlers.rs, heca/src/input.rs, heca/src/actions.rs, heca/src/app/registry.rs, heca/src/app/interaction.rs, heca/src/notification.rs, heca/src/chrome/notification_layer.rs.

---
**Completion summary:**
Follow-up from heca-4b's review: added the "why" to notification_action_relay's ActionDescriptor — it exists because the button can't carry its own Intent at mount time (the notification doesn't exist yet), so it names the relay by id+key (an address, not a smuggled closure) and the relay resolves+dispatches. Everything else unchanged from the prior completion. VERIFICATION: cargo check -p heca clean.

tasks.title: Handle notification dismiss event
tasks.description:
Implementare gli handler delle tre azioni reali `WmAction`: `NotificationDismissOne { id: u64 }`, `NotificationDismissAll`, `NotificationDismissLast` — rimuovere dallo store (una per id, tutte le visibili, o la prima idonea in ordine stabile) e chiedere redraw; nessun accesso UI diretto. Checklist completo AGENTS.md "Adding New Actions" per ciascuna variante — `NotificationDismissOne` non ha keybinding di default (un tasto non può fornire un id), `NotificationDismissAll`/`Last` sì, più RPC e command palette per tutte e tre.

---
**Completion summary:**
SHIPPED: handle_notification_dismiss_one/all/last in heca/src/handlers.rs, each a thin call into NotificationRuntime's dismiss_one/dismiss_all/dismiss_last + state.needs_redraw=true, no direct UI access. Full AGENTS.md "Adding New Actions" checklist done for all three: WmAction variants (input.rs), action_from_name (All/Last only, One needs build_action since it has an arg), build_action (One), action_priority, action_policy=Global, build_registry, ActionRegistry::ALL descriptors, keybindings.default.toml (prefix+Shift+n=Last, prefix+Alt+n=All, One has none by design). RPC: no dedicated rpc.rs code needed — the generic `action <name> key=val` verb (parse_rpc) already reaches any declared action. VERIFICATION: cargo check -p heca clean. NOT verified: nothing visually confirmed (no running app; NotificationDismissOne's mouse path needs T203's mount to exist at all). ReloadConfig) abbiano una policy coerente con dove il bottone può comparire.

SHIPPED: NotificationDismissOne/All/Last and NotificationPick classified ActionPolicy::Global in heca/src/app/interaction.rs (with a spot-check comment explaining why: no layout impact, must stay reachable while a floating pane owns the domain). notify (P055/T491) also Global. Cross-check on "actions referenced by NotificationAction.intent" (e.g. ReloadConfig): those are whatever action the producer names when building the NotificationAction — their own policy is unrelated to and unaffected by living inside a toast; ReloadConfig itself is already Global (pre-existing). tasks.title: Add `notification.pick` action — scoped toast picker
tasks.description:
Toast actions and the × are automatically prefix+/ pickable now (pickability is not opt-in — heca-4b/F003-P096's T486), so every visible toast already competes in the global 52-letter pool via the four hint walks over state.layers.visible_front_to_back() (heca/src/chrome/hint/{surfaces.rs,letters.rs,targets.rs}). Antonio asked for an ADDITIONAL, precise route on top of that — not instead of it: no eligibility exclusion, toast actions keep their global letters too. (Two earlier proposals to exclude the layer from the global pool for a letter-budget saving were both wrong and retracted — MAX_VISIBLE_NOTIFICATIONS=4 already bounds the worst case to 8 of 52 letters, so there is no budget problem to solve; this is purely about precision/convenience.)

Shape (settled with heca-4b, F003/P096): a `notification.pick` action in ActionRegistry (own ActionMeta/descriptor per AGENTS.md:1554's checklist) with a default binding in keybindings.default.toml (user-rebindable). Its handler flips a host-owned `Signal<bool>` — no closures crossing the boundary, just `signal.set(!signal.get_untracked())` or equivalent.

Mount: wrap the ToastStack layer's root (P060/T203) in `KeyHintGroup::new_boxed(stack).open_when(that_signal)`. Do NOT use `opens_on(name)` — that is the focused-surface path (a surface must hold the keyboard for it to fire), and the notification layer is `modal: false` / never focused by design (P060/T203's covers_content:false), so an opens_on binding on it would never trigger. `open_when(Signal<bool>)` is the host-driven equivalent and also holds focus while the group is up, so there is no separate gate to write.

Edge cases: the signal must reset to false when the group closes (Esc / a pick made) so re-pressing the binding reopens cleanly; verify the action doesn't fire while a modal already holds focus (ActionPolicy — cross-check T213, likely Global since it's non-modal/non-layout-affecting, but confirm it doesn't leak into a modal context that should swallow it instead).

---
**Completion summary:**
SHIPPED: WmAction::NotificationPick (name-keyed via action_from_name, zero args), handle_notification_pick toggles state.notification_pick_open (a bool Signal on AppState, additive to global prefix+/, no exclusion). Mount (T203) wraps the toast stack in KeyHintGroup::new_boxed(stack).open_when(state.notification_pick_open). Default binding prefix+n. NOT DONE — flagging honestly rather than closing over it: the "signal must reset to false when the group closes (Esc / a pick made)" edge case this task calls out is NOT implemented. My handler only toggles the bool; nothing resets it when KeyHintGroup itself closes (a pick made, or Esc), so re-pressing prefix+n after a pick would need to flip it back on then off rather than just re-opening. Whether KeyHintGroup exposes a close callback/signal for the host to react to is a heca-grid-ui question — need to ask heca-4b rather than guess or touch his crate. VERIFICATION: cargo check -p heca clean; lint-changed.sh clean (0 warnings in heca). NOT verified: nothing on screen. FILES: heca/src/input.rs, heca/src/actions.rs, heca/src/app/registry.rs, heca/src/app/interaction.rs, heca/src/app_state.rs, heca/src/app/startup.rs, heca/src/handlers.rs, heca/src/chrome/notification_layer.rs, keybindings.default.toml.
